## Lisbon Weekend Trip at a Glance

A comfortable 4-day Lisbon plan for 2 adults, centered in Baixa/Chiado or Avenida da Liberdade to keep walking light and transit easy. I’ve prioritized flat routes, one museum, coffee stops, and rainy-day swaps, with a total target of **EUR 1,400 excluding flights**.

## 4-Day Lisbon Itinerary, Costs, and Low-Impact Routing

| Day | Focus | Main Plan | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Day 1 — Fri, Apr 10 | Old-town arrival | Baixa, Rossio, Chiado cafés, sunset by the river | EUR 210 |
| Day 2 — Sat, Apr 11 | Historic center + museum | Alfama viewpoints with minimal climbing, one museum, tram ride | EUR 320 |
| Day 3 — Sun, Apr 12 | Easy neighborhood day | Belém by taxi/ride-hail, pastries, riverside walking | EUR 290 |
| Day 4 — Mon, Apr 13 | Slow finish | Príncipe Real, coffee hopping, last shopping, departure buffer | EUR 180 |

### Day 1: Easy Arrival in Baixa and Chiado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first walk short around **Baixa** and **Rossio**.
- Afternoon: Coffee stop in **Chiado**; try a classic espresso and a pastel de nata.
- Evening: Flat riverside stroll at **Praça do Comércio** and Cais das Colunas.
- Meal: Simple welcome dinner in Baixa, such as grilled fish, bifana, or petiscos.
- Rainy-day backup: Stay indoors with café hopping in Chiado and covered arcades around Rua Augusta.
- Est. cost: Lodging EUR 160, food/drinks EUR 40, local transit EUR 10.

### Day 2: Alfama Views Without the Steepest Climb
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start by taxi or tram near the top of **Alfama** to reduce uphill walking.
- Afternoon: Visit **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** or **Museu do Fado**; choose one museum only to keep the pace relaxed.
- Evening: Dinner in central Lisbon, then an easy tram ride back.
- Meal: Lunch near the museum, then dinner with bacalhau, soup, or grilled chicken.
- Rainy-day backup: Swap Alfama wandering for the museum plus a long café break in Baixa/Chiado.
- Est. cost: Lodging EUR 160, museum EUR 30, transit EUR 20, food/drinks EUR 110.

### Day 3: Belém Made Comfortable
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Take a taxi or ride-hail to **Belém** to avoid extra walking transfers.
- Afternoon: Visit **Pastéis de Belém**, then a gentle riverside walk near the monuments.
- Evening: Return early and have dinner in the city center.
- Meal: Seafood lunch in Belém, pastries as a snack, light dinner near your hotel.
- Rainy-day backup: Focus on indoor stops like the Coach Museum area or a long lunch-and-coffee break.
- Est. cost: Lodging EUR 160, transit EUR 30, food/drinks EUR 100.

### Day 4: Slow Coffee Finish and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Brunch and coffee in **Príncipe Real** or **Avenida da Liberdade**.
- Afternoon: Short shopping stop, then head to the airport with plenty of buffer time.
- Evening: Keep this flexible for departure.
- Meal: Brunch with eggs, toast, and coffee; light lunch if needed before leaving.
- Rainy-day backup: Use the final hours for a covered café, bookstore, or indoor pastry stop.
- Est. cost: Lodging EUR 0, food/drinks EUR 30, transit EUR 20, buffer EUR 20.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Centrally located lodging | EUR 480 | 3 nights in Baixa/Chiado/Avenida da Liberdade area |
| Food and drinks | EUR 420 | Cafés, lunches, dinners, pastries |
| Local transport | EUR 80 | Mix of metro, tram, taxi, and ride-hail |
| Museum and entry fees | EUR 40 | One museum plus small entries |
| Contingency | EUR 380 | Rainy-day flexibility, nicer dinner, or extra transfers |
| Total | **EUR 1,400** | Excludes flights |

## Best Stay Area and Trip Notes

- **Best lodging zone:** Baixa, Chiado, or Avenida da Liberdade for the flattest access and best transit.
- **Knee-friendly strategy:** Use taxis/ride-hail for Alfama and Belém rather than relying on steep uphill walks.
- **Best museum fit:** **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** for a slower-paced indoor visit.
- **Best coffee zones:** Chiado, Príncipe Real, and Baixa all work well without adding much walking.
- **Most weather-safe day:** Day 2, since it already has the strongest indoor backup.

## Quick Actions
